experience.reason: The sudden shift to visceral body horror and predatory consumption feels tonally disjointed from the preceding psychological melancholy, breaking the thematic consistency of the Voyd as a mirror of desire rather than a physical monster.

The sudden shift to literal, biological imagery ("four small lights... warm and wet") feels tonally jarring and overly concrete compared to the preceding abstract metaphysical horror, breaking the established atmospheric tension. It reads more like a standard survival-horror mechanic than a continuation of the Voyd's conceptual feeding on "wanting," causing a momentary drop in narrative cohesion.

The visceral horror of the body-horror imagery clashes tonally with the preceding thematic focus on regret and erasure, causing a jarring disconnect that breaks the emotional immersion. It feels like a genre shift rather than a deepening of the established psychological stakes.

The sudden invocation of "Orachys" feels like an unearned narrative intrusion that breaks the intimate, psychological tension established in the previous beats, shifting from personal regret to vague lore without sufficient setup.
